direction: A standalone, room-scale AR experience for Specs glasses, viewed first-person at natural eye height over the actual city pavement. The game is a 3 by 3 metre area people walk inside, NOT a miniature board or tabletop prop. Preserve the actual demo's upright camera-facing cyan 1 / amber 2 clues, translucent floor treatment and pale pole red pennant, but simplify and polish the visual hierarchy. No enclosing toy tray, no thick external rail, no chunky corner towers, no raised blue button tiles, no candy materials, no blue plastic surfaces, no dollhouse/isometric camera. A six-by-six floor grid with 50cm cells extends outside the close first-person field of view. Show only the near/middle portion of this larger area; do not shrink the entire grid to fit the image. Clear view of real pavement, no fake black surfaces or lighting. Primary cell cues are thin pale-cyan L-shaped floor corners, tiny quiet registration points and short floor-localized highlights, with generous empty floor. Numbers are substantial readable extruded 3D type 18–22 cm tall at 25–35 cm above the floor, with subtle depth and a very fine connection to their own cell. This is calm, refined spatial information integrated into a real place. Think architectural wayfinding and native spatial computing, not an arcade cabinet, tabletop toy, neon cyberpunk, or a futuristic HUD covering everything.

Create a SIX-FRAME animation storyboard contact sheet: exact 3 columns by 2 rows, no gutters/captions, each cell a square crop of the SAME first-person gameplay view, overall aspect 3:2. The camera stays completely still across all six frames.
INPUT IMAGE 1 is the actual current game screenshot. Preserve its large spatial clue typography, real gray pavement and close first-person room-scale view. INPUT IMAGE 2 shows the actual wider gameplay preview for environmental and real-world scale reference. Treat both as visual references, not as panels to copy.

Specific composition: the viewer is standing inside or at the edge of the play area, looking moderately downward across full-size pavement slabs, with a strip of the real street/buildings visible along the top. Visible floor cells are 50cm wide. The near grid cells extend off the bottom and both sides of the view; distant cells continue across the pavement. Never show an entire small square board surrounded by empty pavement. The gameplay floor occupies the scene, not a prop in the scene. Keep the approved large cyan 1 and amber 2 spatial clues, located in separate cells at multiple real-world depths, and one distant red waving pennant about 35cm high. Minimal pale-cyan floor corner marks define covered cells; safe revealed cells have a short quiet cyan floor edge and their spatial clue. No raised caps or individual physical pads.
SIX FRAMES of one full-scale floor-cell reveal at center foreground: 1 idle sparse floor field with existing clues; 2 four small white corner marks brighten around the cell the player is entering; 3 a very thin floor-plane scan line passes through the selected 50cm cell; 4 the selected cell's blue wash fades away revealing the pavement clearly; 5 a substantial extruded cyan 1 rises to 27cm above that cell, with its fine anchor stem; 6 the clue settles and all floor highlights return to restrained brightness. Only this one cell changes, no board reposition, no camera motion, no big particles.
Keep it spatial, quiet and architectural. All visual content must plausibly use simple real-time Lens Studio meshes, text, transparency and transforms. No outside rectangular board frame, no plastic toy, no dark opaque floor, no angular sci-fi control panels, no tabletop/diorama/isometric view, no candy-like colors, no cinematic shadows/reflections/bloom, no global light cast onto the street. No UI or text other than the clue numerals. Match viewpoint, geometry, grid scale and pavement exactly between cells.

Refinement: remove ALL broad coral/red floor fills present in the reference, including under the distant flag. Quiet thin cyan floor corners and nearly invisible blue tile wash only. The pennant alone is red during normal play.
Now design a serious, clean spatial mine-hit event. One foreground floor cell contains a small 16cm diameter coral faceted spherical Minesweeper hazard with six short squared radial studs and ONE fine pale equatorial seam. It floats 12cm above its floor anchor, with subtle solid front/side shading. No candy stripes, no gumdrop/dome, no toy floor socket, no platforms, no tray, no machinery. The prop is a stylized virtual game token, not a real explosive device; no people near it, weapons, injury, fire or realistic destruction.
SIX DISTINCT POSES: 1 four restrained coral L-shaped corners identify the selected floor cell, no prop yet; 2 the coral studded sphere materializes at the cell center; 3 it briefly compresses and a narrow cream center brightens, a clear instant of anticipation; 4 a small bright cream/coral angular flash briefly occupies the core while eight substantial faceted shards spread outward and upward; 5 the central flash is gone, shards arc and fade, one thin elliptical coral floor ring expands to roughly a single cell radius, the neighboring clues are still legible; 6 no moving debris remains, just a small coral crossed-circle floor marker and a few restrained coral points indicating other mine positions, no red fields. Freeze other clue shapes, locations and flag throughout.
Show body-scale depth through the existing first-person floor perspective and the shallow arc of the pieces. This is a standalone spatial experience, not a tabletop arcade miniature. Real-time plausible low-poly geometry, text, alpha and transforms. No bloom clouds, no screen shake, no cinematic lighting, no cast shadows onto real pavement, no glowing forcefields, no dark opaque surfaces, no extra UI. Keep identical background and camera cropping in all cells. No game-over panel in this sheet.
